action: {"type": "question", "text": "Are the seven repetitions spoken by seven distinct people (or entities), rather than one person repeating the phrase?"}
{"type": "question", "text": "Did one single person say the phrase repeatedly (the same voice uttering it seven times)?"}
{"type": "question", "text": "Are the seven repetitions written text (e.g., printed messages, screens, letters) rather than something spoken aloud?"}
{"type": "question", "text": "Were the seven written messages produced or sent by a single source (e.g., the same sender, device, or author), rather than coming from seven independent origins?"}
{"type": "question", "text": "Are the seven identical written messages electronic/digital (e.g., texts, emails, app notifications) rather than on paper?"}
{"type": "question", "text": "Was the phrase written repeatedly as a punishment \u2014 i.e., the person was made to write it out over and over (like \"writing lines\" as school discipline)?"}
{"type": "question", "text": "Did a single person write and leave seven identical copies of this note to complain about a business or service \u2014 i.e., a customer saying they'll never return?"}
{"type": "question", "text": "Was the phrase written by a human (by hand or typed by a person), rather than produced automatically by a machine or device?"}
{"type": "question", "text": "Is the person who says \"I know I'm in trouble\" the same person who wrote the seven notes?"}
{"type": "question", "text": "Did the writer intend other people to actually read the notes as a real farewell (i.e., meant to make others believe they were leaving for good)?"}
{"type": "question", "text": "Did the writer not genuinely intend to leave, but write the notes so others would believe they were leaving (a hoax, prank, or attention-seeking stunt)?"}
{"type": "question", "text": "Were the seven identical notes given to seven different people, who then compared them (e.g., discovering they'd each received the same message)?"}
{"type": "question", "text": "Did \"I'm never coming back\" mean the writer intended to die (the notes being a suicide/farewell note), rather than simply moving away or ending a relationship?"}
{"type": "question", "text": "Is the writer a child running away from home, who now realizes they're \"in trouble\" for it?"}

{"type": "question", "text": "Is the note addressed to one specific individual person the writer knows personally (e.g., a partner, friend, or family member), rather than an institution, company, or group?"}

{"type": "question", "text": "A wrote the notes himself and is now worried about being \"in trouble.\" Could the seven identical notes be pages/objects in his own possession\u2014for example, seven copies he made for himself rather than messages delivered anywhere? And critically: has the addressee actually seen any of the notes?"}

{"type": "question", "text": "Did the writer never actually give or deliver the notes to their intended reader\u2014so the notes ended up being found by someone else (or otherwise read only after the fact)?"}
{"type": "question", "text": "Is the person to whom the farewell note is addressed the writer's romantic partner or spouse?"}
{"type": "question", "text": "Is the addressee a relative of the writer\u2014such as a parent, sibling, or other family member?"}
{"type": "question", "text": "Did the intended addressee ever actually see or receive any of the seven notes?"}
{"type": "question", "text": "Were the seven identical notes seven separate physical pieces of paper?"}
{"type": "question", "text": "Is the writer a fictional character\u2014that is, does the farewell note appear within a book, story, poem, or published written work?"}
{"type": "question", "text": "Before writing the farewell, had the writer done something that wronged or disappointed the addressee?"}
{"type": "question", "text": "Is the scenario set in an institutional context such as a hospital, prison, school, or workplace?"}

{"type": "question", "text": "Is the \"trouble\" the writer fears a legal or official one \u2014 e.g., being caught by police or an authority \u2014 rather than merely hurting or upsetting the addressee?"}

{"type": "question", "text": "Is the writer planning to fake their own death or disappearance (e.g., to escape debts, claim insurance, or evade responsibility), using the notes as proof they've \"gone for good\"?"}

{"type": "question", "text": "Were the seven identical handwritten copies produced as handwriting specimens/exemplars \u2014 the same sentence written out repeatedly, e.g. for investigators to compare against a note in a case?"}

{"type": "question", "text": "Is the writer about to be imprisoned or sent far away for a long time, so the notes are a real goodbye to that one person \u2014 and the \"trouble\" is a looming punishment?"}
{"type": "question", "text": "Is the writer's legal trouble directly caused by these notes themselves (e.g., the notes are evidence or constitute the offense), rather than unrelated to the notes?"}

{"type": "question", "text": "Is the writer planning to flee or go into hiding from the law (go on the run), with the notes being their real goodbye because they're disappearing from that person's life?"}

{"type": "question", "text": "Is the writer being deported, exiled, or officially banned from the country or place where the addressee lives \u2014 so that \"I'm never coming back\" is literally true and the \"trouble\" is that official action?"}

{"type": "question", "text": "Is the addressee someone the writer is legally responsible for \u2014 a dependent, a minor child, or a patient \u2014 so that walking away (\"never coming back\") would itself be the source of the \"trouble\"?"}
{"type": "question", "text": "Has anyone actually died in this story?"}
{"type": "question", "text": "Did the writer cause that death (directly, through negligence, or in some way be responsible for it)?"}
{"type": "question", "text": "Is the person to whom the farewell note is addressed the same person the writer caused to die?"}
{"type": "question", "text": "Is the writer facing a criminal charge or prosecution from the state for causing the death, rather than only a civil lawsuit or claim?"}
